content.comment_body: While trying to create my first project in this new [product_name] software, the program consistently freezes when I attempt to edit input/output names. This happens even when I only enter information on the initial screen, regardless of whether I provide I/O names. Running it as an administrator made no difference. Is this a known issue with the latest version? It also seems to lock up older projects.
The freezes occur with several actions. Is this problem typical for other users as well?

You may need to update your Java Runtime Environment for compatibility with your operating system. Try installing the latest Java from Oracle and see if that resolves the issue. If not, please provide more details about your PC and operating system.

Surprisingly, disconnecting my external monitor resolved the problem. Using my laptop with an additional monitor seemed to cause [product_name] software to malfunction. After removing the extra monitor, everything worked smoothly. Hopefully this information helps someone else experiencing similar difficulties.

Thank you for sharing your experience. I use an external display via VGA or HDMI when not on-site, but haven't encountered these specific issues. I haven’t yet tried running the software across both internal and external monitors simultaneously. I am aware that certain engineering software can present various problems when extended over dual screens, especially if the application isn’t confined to the primary screen or spans both. Can you confirm whether you were actively using both primary and secondary monitors at the time?

A colleague working with extended desktop setups all day reported that sometimes popup windows will appear only on the primary display, even when the main program is open on the secondary monitor. For example, using the right-click for properties on a circuit diagram under the tools menu occasionally causes confusion if another application is always on top of the visual stack. He notes that there are no serious issues with [product_name] software in his experience (using a standard laptop with Windows 7 and sufficient memory). Does any of this apply to your situation?

I utilized a primary/secondary monitor setup, keeping most applications on the primary screen but dragging the [product_name] environment to the secondary. Only [product_name] and CAD software were used this way, and only [product_name] showed problems. When using ALT-TAB, I noticed an unidentified program with a green arrow and a gray box on the laptop's desktop that couldn't be moved or closed. Nothing in Task Manager explained it, so I hesitated to end processes blindly. Pop-up windows frequently appeared on the primary monitor for both [product_name] and CAD, which was inconvenient but not severe. Allocating 4GB RAM to Java (which is updated) and removing the second monitor permanently resolved my problems. It turned out to be more frustrating than helpful.
Hopefully the developers occasionally see threads like this and consider user experiences. Glad you found a workaround for your issue, and thank you for sharing.

It’s possible the issue arises because the edit input/output names dialog is a modal window, and if it appears on a different monitor, it blocks interactions with [product_name] until closed, making it seem as if the application is frozen. However, I don’t understand why you don’t see the dialog on your other monitor. When testing extended desktop setups, the dialog appeared and could be closed without issue. Is there any application running on your primary monitor that could be hiding the dialog?

I've removed my second monitor, but I used to encounter a gray box on the primary monitor that was inaccessible. It would appear in the ALT-TAB list, but not in the running programs (except for [product_name]). Opening one program on each monitor made no difference. Other software like CAD handled dialog pop-ups without issues, but [product_name] did not. I don't plan to reconnect the second monitor, but if I do, I'll update the thread. Hopefully others won't face this annoyance. Thank you all for your responses!

analysis.insight_summary: Users observed that [product_name] can freeze and lock up, especially when working with dual monitors or editing input/output names. Modal dialogs may sometimes appear off-screen or become inaccessible, causing the interface to seem unresponsive. While other software such as CAD performed reliably in multi-monitor environments, [product_name] experienced issues with window management. This resulted in user frustration due to basic functionality not working as expected.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect [product_name] to remain stable and responsive regardless of monitor configuration, with dialogs consistently appearing and not causing program freezes. Reliable operation in multi-monitor setups is considered standard based on experiences with other professional software.
